what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/judge-words: what each tool does, what it takes and gives back, and how it runs.

payload.label: Check words or anything made against your rules
payload.job: Check words, a plan or anything else someone made against the rules a person set, and say what breaks which rule, why, and what to do instead
payload.description: Give rules (one row each) and what to check: text, texts, value (any JSON whose words a person reads), artifact (any JSON a rule reads by path, like a plan or a take's measures) or items, each with an optional kind. A row picks words (words, pattern, exact or a named grammar check), named groups of markers (groups: a framework's parts, the feelings or cues a script should carry), values (path, with where or where_pattern to keep only some) or an evidence check over supplied evidence (evidence: exact source spans, complete review, a captured answer set), may apply only to some kinds, may judge every item together as one piece (across), and may say what must hold: required, count_at_least, count_at_most, value_at_least, value_at_most, equals, includes_all, in_order, repeated_at_least, percent_found_at_least or together_at_least. Its because and at_most travel with every finding. Each row may carry a weight; the answer's score is the weighted score of the rows that apply, and min_score fails a request scored under it. Returns status (passed, failed, held when only capped rows found something, no-applicable-rule, no-input), score, findings (with the offset of each word found) and lines in plain words. Nothing passes on silence: a value test that finds nothing is a finding.

says.description: Why it matters, in the words the finding shows

suggest.description: What to write or do instead

words.description: Whole words or phrases, any case

exact.description: The whole text is one of these

path.description: A dot path into an artifact; * is one segment, ** any depth

where.description: Keep only the picked values equal to this value or one of this list

when.description: One { path, where } or a list of them: the row applies only to an artifact holding, at every path, a value equal to one of its where (a plan of one format)

kinds.description: The kinds of item the row applies to

fields.description: The keys whose words the row reads

under.description: Only words somewhere under this key

allow.description: A text holding one of these is never flagged by this row

equals.description: Every picked value is one of these

because.description: The records the row came from, carried onto each finding

at_most.description: Present on an inferred row: its findings hold, never fail

label.description: The group's name in a finding's not-found list

words.description: Whole words or phrases that show the group, any case

patterns.description: Regular expressions that show the group, with the row's flags

weight.description: What the group counts for in percent_found_at_least; 1 when it names none

apart_at_least.description: Found only when one marker is in two items at least this many items apart (said again later); needs across

groups.description: Named groups of markers; the row selects each group found

evidence.description: An evidence check over the item's value; the row's other fields are its policy

where_pattern.description: Keep only the picked string values this regular expression matches (with flags)

across.description: True: judge every item the row applies to together, as one piece

normalize.description: Normalize the words before reading them; findings then carry no offset

weight.description: What the row counts for in the score; 1 when it names none

includes_all.description: Each of these values is among the picked values

in_order.description: The picked values in this list come in this order

repeated_at_least.description: Some one picked value is found at least this many times

percent_found_at_least.description: At least this share (0 to 100) of the groups is found, by weight

together_at_least.description: At least this many groups are found in one item; needs across

value.description: Any JSON whose strings a person reads

fields.description: Which keys of value hold words: a list of keys, or "strings" for every string (the default)

paths.description: Only the strings of value at these dot paths

skip_keys.description: Keys of value whose strings are not read

skip_paths.description: Exact dot paths of value that are not read

artifact.description: Any JSON that path rows read, such as a plan or a measure report

items.description: Items to check, each text or value, with its own kind

kind.description: The kind of every item that names none (title, plan, voice take...)

min_score.description: The least score that passes; with none, the score decides nothing

score.description: The weighted score (0 to 100) of the rows that apply

provenance.source: the copy judge parts/judge-words, with kinds, path rows and tests added; the content gate bitfield-packages packages/content-gate merged in as groups, across rows, share, order and repeat tests, weights and evidence checks
